newsitem.title: UK: IGC revises 1997 world wheat crop estimate up.
newsitem.headline: IGC revises 1997 world wheat crop estimate up.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday revised its estimate for 1997 world wheat production up to 579 million tonnes, up from an estimate of 578 million made a month ago.
In its monthly Grains Market Report, the IGC estimated 1996 production at 582 million tonnes.

The small overall change masks a series of moves in either direction. The estimate for India's 1997 wheat crop was revised up to 65 million tonnes from the previous 64 million "Good rains througout the season benefited the crop," the IGC said. And planted area rose in expectation of firmer domestic prices.

There was also a rise for the US, with production now seen at 62.6 million tonnes compared with the previous 60 million. The revision comes after reports of high yields as near perfect weather compensated for earlier freeze losses.

A revision of the total EU crop up to 98.9 million tonnes from the previous 98.7 million includes a change in the UK wheat crop estimate to 16.5 million tonnes from the previous 16.1 million and of the French crop to 35 million tonnes from 34.5 million. Abundant rain in the north of the EU in June promoted plant growth, the IGC said.

On the downside, Canada's estimated production was cut to 25.5 million tonnes from the previous 27 million due to "a major shift to canola, flaxseed and other more profitable crops," the IGC saidf --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
